data.title: Animation
data.tagline: Run a planned sequence of visual changes
data.description: Animation can repeat, play through keyframes, or express a larger state change that a simple transition cannot. Use it to explain progress or spatial relationships, not just to keep the screen moving. Provide a reduced-motion alternative when movement is substantial.

use: Attention to a new but important event
avoid: Loop decorative motion near reading content
Delay a task until an animation finishes
Use movement that conflicts with the interface state

lessonPractice.title: A loading icon spins continuously and stops when complete. Under reduced motion, it should not keep spinning. What is the right approach?

options.label: Use keyframes, start and stop from loading state, and provide static feedback under reduced motion
options.feedback: Autonomous looping suits Animation, state defines its lifetime, and the reduced version preserves information without forced motion.

options.label: Use only transition and make the icon rotate continuously without any property change
options.feedback: A transition requires a property state change and cannot independently define a continuous loop.

options.label: Keep the icon looping after loading so the page continues to feel active
options.feedback: Motion after completion no longer communicates loading, distracts attention, and ignores reduced-motion preference.

data.agentPrompt: Implement the loading spinner with keyframes only while loading. Stop immediately on success or failure and show the resulting state. Under prefers-reduced-motion, use static or weaker feedback, and leave no permanent decorative loop.
